name: Triveni Turbine Ltd
title: Triveni Turbine Ltd - 533655 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 PBT margin fell to 15.7% from 23.5% on weak domestic mix, freight-delayed exports and low-margin NTPC CO2 storage order; order book up only 5.1% to ₹21.8bn, management guides full-year growth but no numbers.

triggers.label: Domestic orders down 35.4% YoY

triggers.quote: The closing order book stood at ₹21.8 billion as of the 30th of June as compared to ₹20.74 billion a year ago, reflecting a 5.1% year -on-year increase.

summary.headline: Triveni Turbine Q1 FY27 revenue rose 19.2% to ₹4.43 bn, but EBITDA margin fell to 18% from 25.8% on export deferrals and low-margin legacy orders.
summary.overview:
Revenue from operations grew 19.2% YoY to ₹4.43 bn, with domestic sales up 27.4% to ₹2.4 bn and exports up to ₹2.03 bn. EBITDA was ₹797 mn (18% margin vs 25.8%) and PBT was ₹697 mn (down 20.1%, 15.7% margin vs 23.5%). Management attributed the margin fall to a higher domestic mix, export deliveries deferred by freight costs rising 3-4x, a near-zero-margin NTPC CO2 energy storage project, and legacy orders priced before commodity inflation. Order booking rose 6.1% to ₹5.68 bn, led by exports and aftermarket, while domestic and product bookings declined.</overview>

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹2.4 bn, up 27.4% YoY, but domestic order booking fell 35.4% YoY and domestic enquiries declined. Management says the domestic market is broadly weak across industries.

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹2.03 bn (48.8% share). Export orders were 68% of Q1 bookings (vs 47%), up 53.4% YoY; exports are 57% of closing order book. Growth is led by Southeast Asia, Africa, Europe and the US.

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: 39% of Q1 order booking (vs 27%), growth of 54% in orders; 29% of closing order book. Driven by geothermal and utility contract wins plus refurbishment.

segments.name: Product
segments.commentary: Product order booking fell 11.6% YoY in Q1.

guidance_outlook: Management is confident of top-line and bottom-line growth for full-year FY27, but growth will be back-ended into H2.
Roughly ₹175 mn of NTPC CO2 project execution remained at end-Q4; management said about 40% falls in Q1 and Q2 with the rest in Q3, while the commissioning is expected around end-Q2 or early Q3.
Management reiterated that a PBT margin above 20% is sustainable in the medium to long term; no specific H2 margin number was given.
US subsidiary is targeted to break even in FY27; product sales from the US are expected to be executed mainly in FY28.
Management expects lumpy quarterly results for a couple more quarters, both positive and negative.
capex_capacity: US facility utilisation in FY27 will be adequate but not high; significant Q1 losses at the US subsidiary were attributed to the absence of an order book.
Execution cycle guidance: under 15 MW about 7-8 months; 15-45 MW about 9-12 months; 30-45 MW about 14-15 months; about 18 months for 100 MW.
Management indicated it is ready to manufacture up to 250 MW class sub-critical packages if NTPC introduces such a policy; participation not yet decided.
Heat pump plus MVR combined solution is in early customer deployment with a demo unit and initial MVR orders in execution; ORC enquiries rising, including in the Americas.
demand_pricing: Export share of Q1 order booking rose to 68%. Management attributed the export execution delays to freight rates rising 3-4x and reduced vessel availability; FOB contracts mean freight is borne by clients.
Domestic enquiries declined. Management said order finalisation is taking longer as customers wait and watch; gestation is 6-12 months.
Bought-out items range 30%-70% of order value depending on the order; all contracts are fixed-price, so commodity inflation during execution is absorbed by Triveni.
US data centre demand is rising as gas turbine lead times extend to 3-5 years; US enquiries have been converted slowly (more than 12 months), with product orders expected first.

Management said the domestic margin decline came from legacy orders booked when commodity prices were volatile and competition was intense, and from lower pricing on the current execution mix. Management expects higher order-booking margins going forward and a rupee benefit.

qa_highlights.question: What was the impact of the NTPC CO2 energy storage order on Q1 margins and quantum?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was taken at negligible or near-zero margin to validate technology, so it adds nothing to profit; about 40% of the roughly ₹175 mn balance is expected in Q1 and Q2, with the rest in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the domestic enquiry trend and reason for the slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give quarterly enquiry numbers, cited weakness in India across industries, flat-to-declining conversations, and longer order gestation periods. Green shoots in Europe and strength in the US and Southeast Asia were noted.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin decline comes from bought-out components and cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Lalit Agarwal said bought-out content varies by order from 30% to 70% of the balance of the order value, and contracts are fixed-price, so commodity increases during execution were absorbed.

qa_highlights.question: What sustainable margin should be expected for H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a specific number, but reiterated that a PBT margin above 20% is achievable over the medium to long term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the US aftermarket and product business?
qa_highlights.answer: The US aftermarket contributed less than 10% of the figure implied by analysts because of state-level certification. US product enquiries are closer to commercial discussions, with product sales expected to lead, followed by refurbishment.

qa_highlights.question: How long are execution cycles for different order sizes?
qa_highlights.answer: Under 15 MW about 7-8 months; 15-45 MW about 9-12 months; 30-45 MW about 14-15 months; about 18 months for 100 MW.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on H2 execution of legacy orders and on the rupee and new orders with higher margins; Q1 PBT margin was 15.7%.
Domestic order booking fell 35.4% YoY and domestic enquiries are declining; the 6-12 month gestation means the effect may appear in later quarters.
Freight costs and vessel availability could defer more export dispatches into Q2 and Q3.
The US subsidiary is loss-making with break-even targeted in FY27; the US product conversion timeline is more than 12 months.
The CO2 energy storage project (with NTPC) is a technology-validation order that has limited profit potential in the early years; commissioning is expected around end-Q2 or early Q3 FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident on full-year growth and H2 recovery, but cautious and somewhat defensive on Q1 margins. Management gave few numbers on enquiries, margin guidance and US timelines, and attributed the weakness to geopolitics, freight and legacy pricing.
